## Study and file layout

The intended observation unit is **one participant**, with baseline and follow-up
measurements in separate columns. The study has 24 participants, with IDs
`"001"` through `"024"`. The export includes one accidentally repeated record.
Identify it by inspecting the data; do not remove records merely because an ID
appears more than once.

The first two lines are descriptive notes. The third line contains column names;
all later lines are records. There are no totals or footer rows. The delimiter
is a comma, the decimal mark is a period, and dates use **year-month-day**.

| Variable | Meaning | Import type and rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Participant identifier | Character; preserve all three digits |
| `arm` | Study arm | Character initially; `control` or `treated` |
| `age` | Age at baseline, in years | Numeric; complete |
| `sbp_baseline` | Baseline systolic blood pressure, mmHg | Numeric after applying the missing-value rules |
| `sbp_followup` | Follow-up systolic blood pressure, mmHg | Numeric after applying the missing-value rules |
| `date_baseline` | Baseline visit date | Character; no date calculation required here |
| `date_followup` | Follow-up visit date | Character; no date calculation required here |

## Missing-value rules

In the blood-pressure columns, `.` and `NM` both mean **not measured**.
Treat both as `NA`; neither means zero. They do not occur in other columns.
A visit date can be recorded even when blood pressure was not measured.

There are no intentionally invalid dates or undocumented numeric corrections.
Do not infer or invent missing measurements.

## Analysis definitions

- Include all unique participants; there is **no age restriction**.
- `change = sbp_followup - sbp_baseline`, in mmHg.
- Change is observed only when **both** measurements are available.
- Negative change indicates a decrease; zero indicates no change.
- Calculate means among participants with observed change. Keep participants
  with missing change in the analysis table and the total participant counts.

These data were constructed for the course, not sampled from a real study.
Arm comparisons are descriptive exercises, not evidence of treatment efficacy.
